svg.title: From Unpaid Judgment to Monthly Payment Stream
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-judgment-assignment-intake-flow; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: From Unpaid Judgment to Monthly Payment Stream; subtitle: Five intake and enforcement steps reported by judgment recovery operators; caption: Operators screen out dead files first, confirm an attachable asset, rate collectibility, open contact by hard-copy letter, then garnish the bank and trade writ dismissal for a down payment plus monthly installments.; assumptions note: Step order combines the operator gates and pro-tips stated by each named practitioner; dollar figures are Rich Meyer's reported terms, not guaranteed outcomes.; note: Sources - TheJRInstitute (3p5TZGrk1og), Default Investor Association with Rich Meyer (fjA8sRRh0ZI), Collect Back Rent Training Course with Cynthia Schmidt (5T2nU_IZTXs).; stages: step: 01; label: Screen Bankruptcy and Death Records; value: Step 1; detail: TheJRInstitute checks bankruptcy filings and death records before preparing the assignment, so no work starts on a dead file.; step: 02; label: Confirm an Attachable Asset; value: Step 2; detail: Rich Meyer confirms an asset exists before signing the creditor, because exemptions such as head of household make wage and bank garnishment difficult.; step: 03; label: Rate and Refuse the Uncollectible 30 Percent; value: Step 3; detail: Cynthia Schmidt rates where the debtor moved, judgment size, and other judgments, and declines the roughly 30 percent she rates uncollectible.; step: 04; label: Mail a PIN Letter Before Any Email; value: Step 4; detail: TheJRInstitute mails a hard-copy letter with a PIN first, then uses that PIN to encrypt every later email to the debtor.; step: 05; label: Garnish the Bank, Then Trade Dismissal for Payments; value: Step 5; detail: Meyer garnishes for $188 and trades writ dismissal for $500 down plus $100 to $200 a month, reaching about $3,000 per month by the third month at ten files a month.

rect.title: step: 01; label: Screen Bankruptcy and Death Records; value: Step 1; detail: TheJRInstitute checks bankruptcy filings and death records before preparing the assignment, so no work starts on a dead file.

text.title: TheJRInstitute checks bankruptcy filings and death records before preparing the assignment, so no work starts on a dead file.

rect.title: step: 02; label: Confirm an Attachable Asset; value: Step 2; detail: Rich Meyer confirms an asset exists before signing the creditor, because exemptions such as head of household make wage and bank garnishment difficult.

text.title: Rich Meyer confirms an asset exists before signing the creditor, because exemptions such as head of household make wage and bank garnishment difficult.

rect.title: step: 03; label: Rate and Refuse the Uncollectible 30 Percent; value: Step 3; detail: Cynthia Schmidt rates where the debtor moved, judgment size, and other judgments, and declines the roughly 30 percent she rates uncollectible.

text.title: Rate and Refuse the Uncollectible 30 Percent
Cynthia Schmidt rates where the debtor moved, judgment size, and other judgments, and declines the roughly 30 percent she rates uncollectible.

rect.title: step: 04; label: Mail a PIN Letter Before Any Email; value: Step 4; detail: TheJRInstitute mails a hard-copy letter with a PIN first, then uses that PIN to encrypt every later email to the debtor.

text.title: Mail a PIN Letter Before Any Email
TheJRInstitute mails a hard-copy letter with a PIN first, then uses that PIN to encrypt every later email to the debtor.

rect.title: step: 05; label: Garnish the Bank, Then Trade Dismissal for Payments; value: Step 5; detail: Meyer garnishes for $188 and trades writ dismissal for $500 down plus $100 to $200 a month, reaching about $3,000 per month by the third month at ten files a month.

text.title: Garnish the Bank, Then Trade Dismissal for Payments
Meyer garnishes for $188 and trades writ dismissal for $500 down plus $100 to $200 a month, reaching about $3,000 per month by the third month at ten files a month.
Assumptions: Step order combines the operator gates and pro-tips stated by each named practitioner; dollar figures are Rich Meyer's reported terms, not guaranteed outcomes.
